A flexible pipe connector (200) for joining a pressurised mains pipe to a service pipe, the connector comprising: • a corrugated longitudinal body portion (202) having a first end (208), a second end (210) and an internal bore therebetween, said longitudinal body portion further comprising a plurality of corrugations spaced along the length thereof, the corrugations defining a maximum internal diameter of the bore at a peak 204 of a corrugation and a minimum internal diameter of the bore at a trough (206) of a corrugation; • a first spigot socket (212) at said first end of the longitudinal body portion; and • a second spigot socket (214) at said second end of the longitudinal body portion; • wherein for a defined volumetric flow rate, the head loss of a fluid flowing through said body portion is no greater than if the fluid were flowing in a smooth bored pipe of the same length and having the same internal diameter as the first and second spigot sockets; and • wherein the minimum internal diameter of said corrugated internal bore is greater than the maximum internal diameter of said first and second spigots.

outputs.L3:
A flexible pipe connector is provided for joining a pressurised mains pipe to a service pipe. The connector comprises a longitudinally extending body having a corrugated wall and an internal bore extending continuously between a first end and a second end of the body. The corrugated configuration allows the connector to flex during installation and use, while maintaining a through-flow path for fluid between the mains pipe and the service pipe.

The corrugations of the body define alternating peaks and troughs along the length of the connector. At the peaks of the corrugations, the internal bore has a maximum internal bore diameter, while at the troughs of the corrugations the internal bore has a minimum internal bore diameter. The connector further includes a first spigot socket at the first end of the corrugated body and a second spigot socket at the second end of the corrugated body. These spigot sockets are configured to receive and connect to corresponding pipe spigots or fittings, thereby enabling the connector to be coupled between the pressurised mains pipe and the service pipe.

The internal geometry of the corrugated bore is selected to reduce flow resistance through the connector. In particular, the corrugated bore is designed such that the head loss through the connector is no greater than the head loss that would occur in an equivalent smooth-bored pipe. Additionally, the minimum internal diameter of the corrugated bore, measured at the troughs of the corrugations, is greater than the maximum internal diameter of the spigots received in the first and second spigot sockets. As a result, the corrugated portion of the connector does not present a constriction relative to the spigots, helping to maintain efficient flow through the connector while still providing the flexibility associated with a corrugated body.
outputs.L4:
A flexible pipe connector is provided for joining a pressurised mains pipe to a service pipe while maintaining effective hydraulic performance. The connector comprises an elongate, flexible body having a longitudinal bore through which fluid can flow. At each end of the body is a spigot socket adapted to receive or connect to a corresponding pipe spigot, fitting, or pipe end. Between the two end sockets, the body is formed with corrugations that allow the connector to bend, deflect, and accommodate misalignment between the mains pipe and the service pipe.

The corrugated portion is designed so that, despite the presence of the corrugations, the internal flow passage remains sufficiently large in comparison with the internal diameter of the end spigots. In particular, the bore through the corrugated section is dimensioned to reduce restriction and turbulence that would otherwise increase pressure loss. The connector therefore provides the mechanical advantages of a flexible corrugated body without creating an unacceptable reduction in flow capacity.

For a specified flow rate through the connector, the head loss produced by the connector is no greater than the head loss that would be produced by an equivalent length of smooth-bored pipe having comparable connection dimensions. As a result, the connector can be used in pressurised water or fluid distribution systems where flexibility is required, for example to compensate for installation tolerances, ground movement, pipe settlement, or angular misalignment, while still preserving the hydraulic efficiency expected from a conventional rigid or smooth-bored pipe connection.

This construction enables a service pipe to be connected reliably to a pressurised mains pipe without the need for precise alignment and without significantly compromising flow performance. The connector is therefore particularly suitable for buried utility applications, water supply connections, and other pressurised pipe systems in which both flexibility and low head loss are important.
outputs.L5:
A flexible pipe is a practical solution for transporting liquids, gases, or other materials in situations where rigid piping is not suitable. Unlike traditional metal or plastic pipes, a flexible pipe can bend, move, and adapt to different spaces, making it useful in both residential and industrial applications.

One of the main advantages of a flexible pipe is its ease of installation. Because it can curve around obstacles and fit into tight areas, it often requires fewer connectors and fittings. This can reduce installation time and lower the risk of leaks. Flexible pipes are commonly used in plumbing, heating systems, ventilation, irrigation, and even offshore oil and gas operations.

Flexible pipes are available in different materials, including rubber, PVC, stainless steel, and composite materials. The right choice depends on the intended use, pressure requirements, temperature resistance, and the type of substance being carried. For example, a flexible pipe used for water supply may need to be corrosion-resistant and safe for drinking water, while one used in industrial settings may need to withstand high pressure or harsh chemicals.

Durability is another important feature. A high-quality flexible pipe can handle movement, vibration, and environmental changes without cracking or breaking. This makes it especially useful in systems where pipes may be exposed to frequent motion or changing conditions.

Overall, a flexible pipe offers convenience, adaptability, and reliable performance. Whether used in a home, garden, factory, or large-scale engineering project, it provides an efficient way to connect systems and transport materials safely.

The intermediate wall portion comprises a plurality of corrugations, including external corrugations (204) and corresponding internal corrugations (206), the corrugations being configured to provide flexibility to the connector (200) while maintaining fluid communication through the connector.
